source: NCERT Class VIII, Our Pasts III, History Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Tribal Societies and their Livelihoods
points: **Tribals ('adivasis')** lived in forests and hills, outside caste society, united by **kinship**.

sub: **Jhum (shifting) cultivators** — cleared and burnt patches to farm (e.g. north-east, central India).

points: '**Diku**' = the tribal word for **outsiders** (traders, moneylenders, officials) seen as exploiters.

sections.heading: 2. How Colonial Rule Affected Tribes
points: The British made tribal chiefs lose their **authority** and forced them to follow British laws and pay tribute.
**Forest laws** declared forests **state property**; **shifting cultivation was banned/restricted**, hurting jhum farmers.
Tribals were pushed into **labour** (tea plantations, mines) and trapped by **traders and moneylenders (dikus)** who charged high interest.
**Reserved forests** stopped tribals from freely using forest produce.

sections.heading: 3. Tribal Revolts and Birsa Munda
points: Anger led to many revolts (e.g. Kols, Santhals, Bastar).
**Birsa Munda** (Munda tribe, Chhotanagpur, 1870s–1900) led a major movement.
He urged tribals to reform (give up drinking, be clean) and to **drive out dikus and the British** to restore a **'golden age' (satyug)** of Munda self-rule.

**Birsa's movement (Ulgulan, 'the Great Tumult')** peaked in **1899–1900**; he was arrested and died in jail (1900). The movement forced the British to pass laws protecting **tribal land** (e.g. the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908).

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Tribals = kinship-based forest/hill communities; livelihoods: jhum, hunting, herding, settled farming.
Colonial forest laws banned shifting cultivation, took forests as state land.
Birsa Munda (Munda, Chhotanagpur) led Ulgulan ('Great Tumult'), 1899–1900; died 1900.
His vision = drive out dikus/British, restore a golden age of self-rule.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Birsa Munda** belonged to the **Munda** tribe (Chhotanagpur); his movement = **Ulgulan** (1899–1900).
Tribes were **kinship-based** and outside the **caste** system.
